gloss: to wash up on shore; to crash against; to surge in

definitions.gloss: to wash up on shore; to beat against; to break (of waves)
definitions.explanation: For waves to roll in and strike the shore, rocks, or a boat. Also used figuratively for crowds or emotions surging forward.

examples.japanese: {波|なみ}が{岸|きし}に{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せる。
examples.english: The waves wash up on the shore.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}きな{波|なみ}が{岩場|いわば}に{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せている。
examples.english: Big waves are crashing against the rocky shore.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}の{影響|えいきょう}で、いつもより{高|たか}い{波|なみ}が{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せていた。
examples.english: Due to the typhoon, waves higher than usual were crashing in.

examples.japanese: ファンの{歓声|かんせい}が{波|なみ}のように{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せた。
examples.english: The fans' cheers surged in like waves.

notes:
Compound of {打|う}つ (to strike) + {寄|よ}せる (to bring close). The literal sense — waves striking the shore — is by far the most common; figurative uses borrow the imagery of a wave.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {波|なみ}が{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せる: waves wash up
- {浜辺|はまべ}に{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せる: to wash up on the beach
- {岩|いわ}に{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せる: to crash against the rocks
- {波|なみ}のように{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せる: to surge in like waves

USAGE:
Most often appears in the present or ている form, describing an ongoing scene. The subject is typically {波|なみ} (waves), but can be other things that move in wave-like motion.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {寄|よ}せる: to draw near — broader; the {打|う}ち prefix adds the impact nuance
- {押|お}し{寄|よ}せる: to surge forward — emphasizes pressure or volume rather than the striking motion

forms.negative: {打|う}ち{寄|よ}せませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {打|う}ち{寄|よ}せていなかった

forms.negative: {打|う}ち{寄|よ}せていませんでした
